statement: Lyons–Peres Conjecture 8.15 asks for critical bond extinction on quasi-transitive G with p_c(G)<1. The 2026-09-24 OpenAI preprint Theorem 1.1 claims the full result; a distinct Lean solution module contains a proof body, while the comparator challenge is a sorry statement stub. This packet does not certify the full proof or trusted-axiom closure.
assumptions: Sources accessed 2026-10-10; public source identity and displayed theorem checked, not full mathematical proof
source: Lyons–Peres Probability on Trees and Networks Conjecture 8.15; https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/No-percolation-at-criticality-on-quasi-transitive-graphs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/math/main/lean/OAI/Probability/CriticalPercolation/Main.lean
source_quote: Theorem 1.1: Let G be an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive undirected graph. If p_c(G)<1, then P_p_c(G)(there is an infinite open cluster)=0.
proof_or_counterexample: Directly compared primary conjecture, preprint theorem and solution/comparator theorem declarations.

statement: In the preprint's adaptive exploration, a uniform bound P(v fails | pretest history)<=delta for each tested site implies P(every site in a fixed finite S is tested and fails)<=delta^|S|, without independence of site outcomes.
assumptions: Sequential tests have a filtration; whether a site is tested and all earlier specified failures are measurable before its test; conditional failure bound holds for tested sites
source: OpenAI, No percolation at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs (2026), Proposition 9.3, equations (59)-(60)
source_quote: For any fixed finite set S of nonroot sites, P(every site of S is tested and fails) <= delta^|S|.
proof_or_counterexample: Order S by test slots. Condition successively on each pretest sigma-field and apply the tower property to multiply the conditional upper bounds; no independence of test outcomes is asserted.
independent_reviewer: w437 independently rederived this step from the preprint
remaining_gap: This only validates the final conditional-product step; freshness and bound (59) still require independent audit.

statement: The w436 dyadic-burst tree has maximum degree 9 and p_c=1/2, yet its root survives at criticality with probability at least 4/5; the tree is not quasi-transitive.
assumptions: 8 children at powers-of-two generations and 2 otherwise; iid bond states
proof_or_counterexample: Independent offspring second-moment recurrence gives normalized second moment <=5/4 at p=1/2, so Cauchy-Schwarz and continuity give survival >=4/5; first moment below 1/2 rules out survival; unique degree-8 root forces infinitely many orbits.
remaining_gap: Boundary example lies outside quasi-transitive class; no parent-problem conclusion.

statement: For the d-regular tree, d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1) and critical clusters are finite almost surely although the root's expected critical cluster size is infinite; the expected count within radius N is 1+Nd/(d-1).
assumptions: Infinite d-regular tree and iid Bernoulli bond percolation
source: owner-own-work:w435/ATTEMPT.md L5; Hutchcroft arXiv:1605.05301v1 Theorem 6; prior C0084-A001 in 2026-09-07 attempts.jsonl line 72
source_quote: Theorem 6 says expected cluster size is finite for every p<p_c; the prior attempt speculated finite susceptibility at p_c in a spherically-averaged sense.
proof_or_counterexample: There are d(d-1)^(n-1) vertices at level n, each linked to root with probability p_c^n, giving d/(d-1) per level; Tonelli diverges. Critical Bin(d-1,p_c) Galton–Watson branches become extinct almost surely.
remaining_gap: Corrects the prior inference but does not settle the general conjecture.
